question.text: The length of the chord of the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{4}+\frac{y^2}{2}=1$, whose mid-point is $\left(1, \frac{1}{2}\right)$, is :

solution.text:
$\begin{aligned}
& T=S_1 \\
& \frac{x \cdot 1}{4}+\frac{y}{4}=\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8} \\
& \Rightarrow 2 x+2 y=3 \\
& \frac{x^2}{4}+\frac{\left(\frac{3-2 x}{2}\right)^2}{2}=1 \\
& \Rightarrow x=\frac{12 \pm \sqrt{120}}{12} \Rightarrow y=\frac{1}{2} \mp \frac{\sqrt{120}}{12}
\end{aligned}$

So length of chord
$=\frac{2 \sqrt{15}}{3}$
